main_body: Cottage: a large tiled roof slope (rows 2-42) over a timber-framed plaster front wall (rows 44-78) with a door, a window and a stone base
top_band: Terracotta roof slope from row 2 to row 42, light orange at the top shading to dark red-brown at the eave; a dark eave line sits at rows 41-42
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the tiled roof slope is a big foreshortened top surface with a gradient and a chimney, much like the Beodeul house roofs. A dark eave band at rows 41-42 marks the front edge and casts a shadow onto the wall. Below it is the vertical plaster wall with timber framing. The door has a stone frame and the window has a dark upper inner edge, shutters and a sill, so both read as inset. No receding side face is drawn. The roof is a plain front-facing slope with no ridge or gable, but it still clearly reads as a top surface above a separate front face.

style.evidence: The roof has about 6 tones, with per-tile highlights, dark joints and a gradient from light to dark, close to the reference tiles. Outlines are tinted: dark brown beside the wood, dark red-brown beside the roof, grey-violet on the stone. The plaster wall has speckle and the timber has grain, but the cream wall areas are fairly large and calm, so some tiles carry fewer colours than the reference. The overall craft is acceptable next to the reference and does not look sticker-like.
